result:
Round r0003 red-team work is done: 9 new findings (F-0021 to F-0029), with the verdict in `work/board/r0003/redteam.json`. I only wrote in `work/agents/redteam/`, `work/findings/` and my own verdict file. I planted no canaries this round.

**Critical**
- **F-0021: the friction shortcut the PI chose on 2026-10-27 underestimates the friction needed by 1.4–2.8×.** This is the "friction needed to hold" number (mu_req, from `methods/e02_friction_limit.py`).
  - **Cause:** the cage is glued to the bone in the model, and at peak load 38–47 % of the glued face is pulling on the bone, which a real interface cannot do. The script drops the pulling elements but keeps the compressed side in full, so it counts total compression of 1.4–2.8 times the net force pressing the face.
  - **p062, extension, bottom face:** 0.119 becomes 0.328 (0.468 once the out-of-plane shear is kept), so the verdict flips from "holds" to "slips" at the main friction value of 0.3.
  - **Lateral bending:** 0.611 becomes 1.082.
  - The scaled correction for the twist part is only approximate; the force-ratio correction is exact.
  - Until this is fixed, designs should not be ranked by this number (`r0003_tension.py`).

**Major**
- **F-0022: the new slip-out rule can be gamed.** It best-fits one rigid motion to all cage nodes, so it measures how much of the cage moves, not how far. All of these pass on a p062-sized test cage:
  - a 10° spin that moves the corners 1.2 mm;
  - the back 10 % sliding 4.5 mm toward the spinal cord (reported as 0.48 mm);
  - the front 25 % pushing 3.5 mm out of the disc space (reported as 0.88 mm). Nothing checks that the cage stays in the disc space after loading.
  - `PLAN.md` still uses the old cage-centre rule, and neither rule exists as code.
- **F-0024: gradual walking is invisible.** Small local slips can add up over cycles into whole-cage migration without the cage ever sliding as a whole (Pai & Hess 2002, *Engineering Failure Analysis* 9:383-402). The friction simulation runs only 3 cycles on a few designs. Applying this to the cage is an analogy; I specified a test but did not run it.
- **F-0023: no verification gate tests the path that now gives the deciding number.**
  - Nothing tests glued contact.
  - The friction-limit script was only checked on flat discs.
  - The new Newton solver has passed only a friction test that never slides and a flexion run with zero facet-joint force.
- **F-0025: the governance rules are being skipped.**
  - Round 3 started even though the verifier's round 2 verdict was HOLD.
  - None of the 20 earlier findings has a reply, and F-0011 to F-0020 aren't in git.
  - `GOVERNANCE.md` still says role permissions are enforced, but every role now has full access.
  - The solver code changed while I was reading it; I saved a snapshot in `r0003_snap/`.
  - There is no digest for this round.
- **F-0026:** `VERIFICATION.md`, `METHODS_COMPARISON.md` ("safe for sure"), `PLAN.md` S9 and `ISSUES.md` are out of date and overstate what has been shown.
- **F-0029:** a fifth agent, the "foreman", was added mid-round. It can edit the round runner and restart or re-queue runs. It checks no code version and nobody audits what it does.

**Minor**
- **F-0027 (issue I-001) is refuted again.** The rerun output was identical to round 2. Flexion twist is at most 1.1 N mm, and left and right lateral bending match (91.1 vs 91.0 N mm). Still open:
  - The p014 rerun crashed partway, so it has no lateral bending or axial rotation data, and nobody has recorded why.
  - Axial rotation is now the direction that sets the required friction.
- **F-0028:** in the solver code being edited, the contact force and the Newton solver's search direction follow different rules when friction is on. This can make friction runs fail to finish rather than give wrong numbers.

The scripts and arithmetic are in `work/agents/redteam/r0003_notes.md`.

Sources:
- [Pai & Hess 2002 (via review, doi 10.3390/machines11020212)](https://doi.org/10.3390/machines11020212)
- [US9995343B2 Rolling bearing (outer-ring creep)](https://patents.google.com/patent/US9995343)
- [WCECS 2013 pp.1030-1035](https://www.iaeng.org/publication/WCECS2013/WCECS2013_pp1030-1035.pdf)
